bib.title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)

question: Can an LLM planner compose a wide, heterogeneous set of tools (LLMs, vision models, web search, Python, rule-based) into natural-language programs for knowledge-intensive reasoning without any training?
hypothesis: An in-context LLM planner that synthesizes sequential natural-language programs over a richer tool inventory generalizes CoT and PoT and outperforms them.
contributions: A plug-and-play compositional reasoning framework, Chameleon, that composes external tools to address LLM limitations
An LLM as natural-language planner that integrates LLMs, off-the-shelf vision models, web search engines, Python functions and rule-based modules
Effectiveness on ScienceQA and TabMWP, significantly surpassing the state of the art

method.summary: A training-free system: an LLM planner (gpt-3.5-turbo or gpt-4), prompted with module descriptions, constraints and few-shot examples, emits a sequence of module names (a natural-language program); modules are bound by string matching and executed sequentially over a query and a cache updated by hand-written update_input/update_cache functions. Evaluated on ScienceQA and TabMWP with task-specific module subsets.
method.task: multi-modal science QA (ScienceQA) and tabular math word problems (TabMWP)

inference.max_tokens: planner program 128; LLM modules default 512; Query Generator 64; TabMWP Row Lookup 256, Column Lookup 256, Program Generator 256
inference.samples: 1 run per item, no seeds or repeats stated (inferred: temperature 0, single pass)
inference.prompting: Planner: instruction plus module descriptions plus few-shot question-to-module-sequence examples. LLM modules default four in-context examples. ScienceQA: Knowledge Retrieval 3, Solution Generator 2. TabMWP: Knowledge Retrieval 5, Row Lookup 7, Column Lookup 6, Table Verbalizer 7, Solution Generator 16.
inference.retrieval: Bing Search API returns top three responses; Knowledge Retrieval is LLM-generated, not an index

parameters.invalid-program fallback ScienceQA: default to Solution_Generator then Answer_Generator if not the final two elements
parameters.invalid-program fallback TabMWP: default to Program_Generator, Program_Verifier, Program_Executor, Answer_Generator
parameters.TabMWP constraints: must include Answer_Generator; Program_Generator before Verifier and Executor
parameters.Row Lookup enabled when: more than three rows and 18 table cells
parameters.Column Lookup enabled when: two or more columns and 18 or more cells
parameters.Answer Generator: rule-based; two-place precision for numeric answers; most similar option for multiple choice

baselines: Fine-tuned: MCAN, Top-Down, BAN, DFAF, ViLT, Patch-TRM, VisualBERT, UnifiedQA, MM-CoT, LLaMA-Adapter, TAPEX
Few-shot GPT-3, GPT-3 CoT, GPT-3 CoT-PromptPG, Codex PoT-SC
eval.protocol: Single test-set evaluation; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported. Ablation on 500 test examples with ChatGPT. Error analysis on 50 ChatGPT-mistake ScienceQA examples.

limits: Authors concede: evaluated on only two benchmarks; planner quality may drive performance; the program is generated in one step with no re-planning; the module list and descriptions must fit in the LLM context window (Appendix B).
Failure cases: weak tool outputs (poor search query, weak captioner), suboptimal plans, and missing tools such as arrow parsing in food webs (Tables 19-24).
No seeds, variance, significance tests, cost or latency reported; planner and modules rely on closed OpenAI models (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4) and Bing, so rerun depends on deprecated engines.
Ablation uses 500 test examples with ChatGPT only.
Broader impacts: misinformation and privacy risks if tools and data sources are not curated; over-reliance on autonomy (Appendix C).
No tool-call safety, sandboxing or permission discussion for Python execution; Program Verifier is an LLM check.
